title: Mountains, Rivers and Lakes of the World

cards.h: The prelims map of the world
cards.b: Prelims and mains ask for the highest peaks, longest rivers, biggest lakes and where they are. These are also the ingredients of regional geography answers. Learn them as a short list for each continent, with one fact each.

Himalaya-Karakoram (Asia): Everest 8,849 m (2020 survey: 8,848.86 m). Andes (South America): the longest continental range at about 7,000 km, Aconcagua 6,961 m. Rockies (North America): Mt Elbert. Alps (Europe): Mont Blanc. Urals: the Europe-Asia divide. Atlas (Africa). Great Dividing Range (Australia): Mt Kosciuszko. Drakensberg (South Africa).

• Asia: Everest, 8,849 m.
  • South America: Aconcagua, Argentina.
  • North America: Denali (Mt McKinley), Alaska.
  • Africa: Kilimanjaro, Tanzania, 5,895 m.
  • Europe: Mt Elbrus (Russia), 5,642 m.
  • Antarctica: Vinson Massif.
  • Oceania: Puncak Jaya (Carstensz Pyramid), or Kosciuszko for the mainland.

The Nile (about 6,650 km, Africa, to the Mediterranean) and the Amazon (about 6,400 km, with the largest water volume; measures disputed) lead. Then the Yangtze, Mississippi-Missouri, Yenisei, Yellow River, Ob, Congo, Mekong, Amur and Lena. The Congo is the deepest river and the only one to cross the equator twice.

The Nile has White and Blue tributaries joining at Khartoum, ends in a bird's foot-like fan delta and feeds Aswan High Dam (Lake Nasser). The Danube crosses ten countries. The Rhine is Europe's busiest waterway. The Volga is Europe's longest river and flows into the Caspian. The Tigris and Euphrates join as Shatt al-Arab. The Colorado carved the Grand Canyon.

Caspian Sea: the largest enclosed water body (saline). Superior: the largest freshwater lake by area, North America. Victoria: Africa's largest, source of the White Nile. Baikal: deepest (about 1,640 m) and oldest, holds about 20 percent of unfrozen fresh water. Tanganyika: second deepest. Aral Sea: shrank due to irrigation. Dead Sea: lowest land surface, about 430 m below sea level.

Tectonic or rift lakes (Tanganyika, Baikal, Dead Sea). Glacial lakes (Great Lakes). Volcanic crater lakes (Lake Toba, Crater Lake). Oxbow lakes. Salt lakes in dry zones (Great Salt Lake, Lake Eyre). Lagoons. Understanding the origin lets you place a lake even if you forget the name.

The Aral Sea lost over 90 percent of its area after rivers were diverted for cotton from the 1960s. Lake Chad has shrunk. The Dead Sea falls by about a metre a year. The Mekong faces dam impacts. The Colorado often no longer reaches the sea. These are stock examples for questions on water stress.

Highest lake: Gurudongmar (Sikkim). Largest freshwater lake: Wular (Kashmir). Largest salt lake: Chilika (brackish lagoon). Pangong Tso straddles the Line of Actual Control. India's Himalaya feeds the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra, parts of the Third Pole that shape rivers shared with Pakistan, China, Nepal and Bangladesh.

Likely questions: 'Locate on the map: Lake Baikal, Danube, Aconcagua', 'Why is the Nile important to Egypt?', 'Drying of the Aral Sea'.

  • Memorise one superlative per feature.
  • Use a quick sketch map in mains with 5-6 labels.
  • Link to human impact: dams, irrigation, shared basins.
